So the bound decays like 2^(-c·d) with c = (1/2)·log₂(2π/e) ≈ 0.6044.","why_clearer":"It removes the awkward `-(1/2) * logb 2 (2π/e)` and writes the limit as a plain positive multiple of log₂(e/(2π)), the same quantity that appears in the sqrt(e/(2π)) limit of the companion theorem."}

parsed.restated: Tendsto (fun d : ℕ => Real.logb 2 (PackingBounds.fullLinearProgram d) / (d : ℝ)) atTop (nhds ((1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (Real.exp 1 / (2 * Real.pi))))
parsed.proof:
have h : (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) * Real.logb 2 (2 * Real.pi / Real.exp 1) = (1 / 2 : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (Real.exp 1 / (2 * Real.pi)) := by
  have h2 : Real.exp 1 / (2 * Real.pi) = (2 * Real.pi / Real.exp 1)⁻¹ := (inv_div _ _).symm
  rw [h2, Real.logb_inv]
  ring
rw [h]
parsed.english: The binary logarithm of the linear-programming bound, divided by d, converges to (1/2)·log₂(e/(2π)), a negative number. So the bound decays like 2^(-c·d) with c = (1/2)·log₂(2π/e) ≈ 0.6044.
parsed.why_clearer: It removes the awkward `-(1/2) * logb 2 (2π/e)` and writes the limit as a plain positive multiple of log₂(e/(2π)), the same quantity that appears in the sqrt(e/(2π)) limit of the companion theorem.
